answer: Remote online notary seals turn an agent from a faceless cipher into one person a commissioned notary has met on camera. First, the operator joins a 10-minute video call and passes a credit-history quiz. Second, the notary checks a passport, records the session, and signs a seal over the agent key. Third, the registry hashes the journal entry and rejects a second seal for the same person. 1,000 sybils need 1,000 real IDs at about $60 each plus a $25 fee per session, $85,000, and each fake is a filmed felony. Faking one is like selling dyed canyon sandstone as jade: one scratch shows it.
